bull.b: Fast Track status and encouraging early immunogenicity data support continued advancement of ACI-7104. U.S. trial expansion may improve development efficiency and strengthen AC Immune’s proprietary Parkinson’s franchise over the next several years.

The Takeda agreement validates AC Immune’s active-immunotherapy platform and provides potential non-linear future economics. Milestones, royalties and partner funding can reduce development burden while preserving upside from successful commercialization.

Low debt limits fixed financial obligations, while reported cash reserves provide meaningful time to advance clinical assets. This runway can reduce immediate financing pressure and allow management to pursue milestones before seeking additional capital.

bear.b: AC Immune remains dependent on external funding because clinical R&D costs exceed internally generated revenue. Continued losses and renewed cash burn could consume reserves faster than planned and increase reliance on partnerships, grants or equity issuance.

Revenue is small and volatile because it depends heavily on collaboration funding, milestone timing and deferred income recognition rather than product sales. This limits forecasting visibility and may create uneven resources for wholly owned development programs.

bear.t: Shrinking equity cushion and financing risk
bear.b: The substantial decline in equity reduces the balance-sheet cushion available to absorb continued development losses. Although the capital band increases financing flexibility, future equity raises could dilute existing holders and signal ongoing funding needs.
